exposure: secondary MSAF (clear amnionic fluid that transitioned to MSAF during labor)
primary MSAF (MSAF present at membrane rupture)
outcome: low one- and five-minute Apgar scores
composite adverse neonatal outcome (arterial cord blood pH <7.1, 5 min Apgar score ≤7, and/or neonatal intensive care unit admission)
cohort: 56,863 singleton term births at a single tertiary medical center in Israel between 2011 and 2018
finding: Secondary MSAF was independently associated with an increased risk of composite adverse neonatal outcome compared with primary MSAF.
mod_finding: Secondary MSAF compared with primary MSAF increased the risks of cesarean birth and operative vaginal delivery.
